chunks: "An obligatory salat (prayer) is better than twenty hajj pilgrimages, and one hajj pilgrimage is better than a house filled with gold that is given in charity in righteousness until it is exhausted."
Then he said: "And no one prospers who wastes twenty houses of gold over twenty-five dirhams."
So it was said to him: "What is the meaning of twenty-five dirhams?" He said: "Whoever withholds zakat, his salat (prayer) is suspended until he pays zakat."

key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: the obligatory alms-tax due on wealth
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a monetary unit indicating a small amount of wealth
key_terms.ذَهَبًا: gold given as wealth or charity

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about the relationship between salat and zakat?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the immense merit of obligatory salat (prayer), placing it above repeated hajj, and hajj above vast voluntary charity. It also warns that withholding zakat invalidates spiritual success and causes one’s salat to be suspended until the zakat is paid. The narration highlights the inseparable connection between acts of worship and financial obligation.
